accuracy: Distances are 1/parallax with no prior; 98.3% of m10 rows use Gaia DR3. Equinox J2000.0; epoch J2000.0 except Tycho-2 stars with pflag X and no Hipparcos match (epoch J1991.5, per the build notes). AT-HYG's ACKNOWLEDGMENTS list neither SIMBAD nor Høg et al. 2000 although its build notes use both; both are credited here.
adaptations: Positions turned into ICRS Cartesian parsecs from ra, dec and dist; V derived from Tycho VT as V = VT - 0.090 (BT-VT), the formula in AT-HYG's own build notes, for 209,908 rows; absolute magnitudes recomputed as V + 5 - 5 log10 d with no extinction correction; colour indices and spectral types turned into display temperatures; 209,156 stars within 500 pc with parallax/error > 10 packed into deep.bin (pc x 64 in int16, M_V in 0.1 mag steps). The shipped star files are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.
licence_quote: "This work is licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License][cc-by-sa]." (LICENSE)
source: Compiled from Tycho-2 (Høg et al. 2000) and its first supplement, Hipparcos (ESA 1997, 2007 reduction via HYG), Gaia DR3 and DR2 parallaxes (ESA/Gaia/DPAC, from gaiadr3.gaia_source_lite and SIMBAD look-ups), the Yale Bright Star Catalog, the Gliese & Jahreiss 1991 nearby-star catalogue, the Tycho-2 Spectral Type Catalog (Wright et al. 2003) and SIMBAD cross-identifications (CDS, Strasbourg).
title: AT-HYG v3.2 (Augmented Tycho-HYG), subsets athyg_32_reduced_m10 and athyg_32_hyg_ids

accuracy: Parallax errors of the Gaia DR3 stars in deep.bin, read from Stellarium's copy (stored in 0.01 mas steps) at build time: median 0.02 mas, 90th percentile 0.07 mas. No zero-point correction.
adaptations: Used only as the distances AT-HYG already carries; no Gaia file is read directly.
licence: Unresolved: ESA's licence page could not be read from the build network. Celestia and celestia-gaia-stardb files state CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO, a third-party PyPI package states CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, the AWS Open Data registry says "Attribution required". Treat Gaia-derived values as non-commercial until confirmed.

Funding for the DPAC has been provided by national institutions, in particular the institutions participating in the Gaia Multilateral Agreement." (AT-HYG ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md)
owner: European Space Agency (ESA), Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC)
source: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023; parallaxes as carried by AT-HYG v3.2
title: Gaia Data Release 3 (inside AT-HYG distances)

accuracy: Gliese 1991 distances are often photometric: of the 574 Gliese-only stars within 20 pc that AT-HYG matched to Gaia DR3, 72% agree within 20% and 5% are off by more than a factor of two (measured on these files).
adaptations: Used for the 661 HYG rows AT-HYG does not carry: Gliese companions (at their primary's AT-HYG distance along their own direction, flag bit 2) and Gliese-only stars (at their Gliese 1991 distance, flag bit 6); spectral types filled in for 971 AT-HYG rows that had none; HIP 55203 (xi UMa, deleted in HYG v3.5) mapped to HYG's xi UMa A.
licence_quote: "The licensing for HYG v4.0 is Creative Commons CC BY-SA 4.0, unlike previous versions of the HYG catalog." (hyg/version-info.md)
source: Hipparcos (ESA 1997; 2007 new reduction), Yale Bright Star Catalog 5th ed. (Hoffleit 1991), Gliese & Jahreiss 1991 (CNS3 preliminary); IAU WGSN names.
title: HYG database v4.1 (hygdata_v41.csv)

accuracy: Parallax stored in 0.02 mas steps; the catalogue author calls the files experimental.
adaptations: Nothing shipped. Each AT-HYG star was joined by Gaia DR3 id or HIP number to read a parallax error. The error qualifies AT-HYG's distance only when both come from the same Gaia DR3 source (332,286 rows) or when the two parallaxes agree within 3 sigma (1,733 rows); 2,951 rows with a distance have no applicable error.
licence: No data licence stated; the files sit in a GPL-2.0-or-later source tree
licence_quote: COPYING: "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 2, June 1991"; no data-specific notice.
owner: Stellarium team; catalogues built by Henry Leung (henrysky/stellarium_star_catalogs)
source: Gaia DR3 (ESA/Gaia/DPAC) and Hipparcos values via SIMBAD
title: Stellarium v26.2 hip_gaia3 star catalogues 0-3 (build-time check only, not shipped)

accuracy: Figures are a drawing convention, not a measurement; IAU constellations are defined by their boundaries.
adaptations: 752 unique figure segments resolved to named rows, 30 of them kept for the sky view only because a star has no usable parallax; 525 IAU names attached, 9 have no row in AT-HYG/HYG.
source: Constellation figures from the IAU "The Constellations" pages (Sky & Telescope: Roger Sinnott, Rick Fienberg, Alan MacRobert); star names from the IAU Catalog of Star Names (IAU WGSN).
title: Stellarium v26.2 sky culture "modern_iau"

accuracy: As of the pinned commit, and not complete: no planet is listed for Barnard's Star, and eps Eridani b is "Controversial", so it is not shown.
adaptations: Planets listed as "Confirmed planets" only: 1,255 planets on 889 named rows. Hosts joined to AT-HYG/HYG by identifier or by position (<= 30 arcsec, distance within 5%); 167 hosts within 100 pc placed from the catalogue's own coordinates and distance; values rounded to 4 significant digits.
licence_quote: "The database is licensed under an MIT license (see below), which basically says you can do everything with it." (README.md)
source: Community-curated compilation (Rein 2012, arXiv:1211.7121); most recent entries imported from the NASA Exoplanet Archive.
title: Open Exoplanet Catalogue

accuracy: A dwarf sequence applied to every luminosity class; display use only.
adaptations: Bt-Vt and spectral-type columns interpolated to effective temperature for display colours; only the derived colour table ships.
licence: No licence stated on the table (the MeanStars code is BSD-3-Clause)
licence_quote: "that reference should be cited until an updated version of the table is published" (file header)
source: Pecaut & Mamajek 2013, ApJS 208, 9 (Table 5); the copy bundled in the MeanStars 3.6.1 wheel on PyPI
title: A Modern Mean Dwarf Stellar Color and Effective Temperature Sequence, v2022.04.16

accuracy: A blackbody-based model. It underestimates hot stars: B-V = -0.215 gives 13,957 K where Mamajek's B2V row has 20,600 K; at the Sun's B-V of 0.65 it gives 5,778 K (Mamajek G2V: 5,770 K).
adaptations: T = T0 (1/(a BV + b) + 1/(a BV + c)) with the coefficients read from the pinned source: a = 0.92, b = 1.7, c = 0.62, T0 = 4600; used for 10,399 named and 78,936 deep stars.
owner: F. J. Ballesteros; coefficients as coded in PyAstronomy 0.25.0 (MIT)
title: B-V to effective temperature (Ballesteros 2012, EPL 97, 34008) — a model

accuracy: The chromaticity of an ideal blackbody; real stellar spectra differ, most for M stars.
adaptations: Planck spectra integrated against the CMFs at 1 nm, converted with the IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB matrix and normalised to the largest channel.
licence: Standard reference data; colour-science is BSD-3-Clause
licence_quote: colour-science LICENSE: "Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without modification, are permitted..."
title: CIE 1931 2-degree standard observer colour-matching functions
